newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Nov 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Nov 20.

text.p: The caretaker National Party government had kept coalition talks with New Zealand First on track by yielding to Maori MPs' demands that it back off supporting claims by urban Maoris for fisheries assets in a Privy Council hearing beginning on Monday, sources said. The government had intended to support a controversial Court of Appeal ruling that urban Maoris were a tribe entitled to benefit directly from Maori fisheries assets. It is understood from sources within political, Maori and legal circles that NZ First's Maori MPs said unless the Crown Law Office pulled back to a neutral position they would refuse to endorse a coalition deal with National. Page 1.

NZ First leader Winston Peters on Monday dismissed as mindless speculation suggestions that NZ First had a favoured coalition partner. Peters said NZ First was still dealing with both Labour and National on an even footing. He said speculation would not affect the talks but he wanted to reassure Labour and National that it did not come from NZ First. Labour leader Helen Clark said installing deputy leader Michael Cullen as finance minister in any coalition agreement remained a non-negotiable condition. Page 2.

Weaker-than-expected wages data put an easing of monetary policy back on track, though economists are mixed on the chances of a cut in rates next month. Bankers Trust economist Nick Bennenbroek said the two risks to an easing in December had been wage rises and a new government changing fiscal outlook. The wages data on Tuesday effectively removed one of those risks. On Monday, Statistics NZ said average ordinary time earnings rose 0.7 percent in the three months to August, for a 3.4 percent annual rise. However, it was the private sector wages growth that was most positive for the inflation outlook - coming in well below expectations at 0.3 percent and 3.7 percent respectively. Page 18.

Listed Asian Properties has been told to produce the documents at the centre of a long-running dispute with 18.9 percent shareholder Hetherington. The Court of Appeal this week granted Hetherington's application for discovery over a property in London's Belgravia district, motor vehicles acquired by the company and other matters. Page 18.

Intense competition for stock, coupled with lower returns from associated products cut the bottom line of meat company Richmond by $1 million for the year to September, chairman Sam Robinson said on Monday. Richmond's consolidated tax-paid profit for the year was $7.5 million. Page 18.

The former Skellerup Group has sold off the Levene paint manufacturing business to ICI for an undisclosed sum. ICI is expected to become the biggest paint maker in New Zealand when it buys the business on December 2 from Maine Investments. Page 18.

New Zealand needs a cheaper currency to stay competitive in export markets, according to Tony O'Reilly, the Irish media magnate and international food giant,Heinz, chairman. "One of the things we have learned as exporters here through Watties is the enormous difficulty of selling New Zealand goods abroad at the US 71 cents level," O'Reilly said. Page 19.

Bancorp Holdings has advocated the issuing of a monthly consumer price index, arguing that the economy was being held to ransom while the Reserve Bank waited for economic data to be made available. Page 21.

Australian Liquor Marketers, a leading Australian liquor wholesaler, is to enter the New Zealand market by taking over the distribution network, about 60 staff and the warehouses of New Zealand Wines and Spirits. Page 24.

Plans for new motor vehicle safety standards have upset both new-car makers and the importers of used vehicles from Japan. New Zealand's vehicle safety standards, mostly set in 1990, lag behind Australia, Europe and the United States and an update has been planned for three years.

NZ First leader Winston Peters indicated on Monday he expects to have no say over the MPs his coalition partner chooses for the cabinet. Nor would Peters expect a coalition partner to decide which NZ First MPs entered the cabinet. Peters was also adamant NZ First was not favouring National. And he confirmed that at the end of the process he aimed to have two complete agreements with both parties for his caucus to choose between.

The Meat and Wool Boards have to improve their performance in the next three to five years or refund the $280 million they hold in farmer reserves, says caretaker Agriculture Minister Lockwood Smith. He said he sympathised with farmer demands for a better return on the capital, which has been built up to fund promotion and spending on research and development.

Power New Zealand has let its major council shareholders off a hook preventing them from selling their key seven percent stake to Mercury Energy. Mercury and Power New Zealand continue to differ, however, on whether that leaves the councils free to dispose of their shares as they wish.

Overheated betting on Sky City's fortunes was confirmed on Monday as a leading broker tempered its profit forecasts. The June 1997 year earnings downgrade from $47 million to around $40 million sent the casino company's shares tumbling 28 cents to 805 cents. The range of estimates for various brokers is now between $39 million and $45 million. First NZ Capital - the lead broker in the Sky City listing at the beginning of the year - said it had been a little optimistic in its projections.
Weaker-than-expected wages data and further issues of New Zealand dollar-denominated bonds drove the dollar higher and wholesale interest rated lower in quiet trading on Monday.

The New Zealand dollar will reach a new peak of about US72.25 cents in the next few months and then reverse into a bear market that could develop into a collapse to new lows within six years, according to ANZ Bank chartist Mark Elliott. He said on Monday that many commmentators agreed the kiwi was over-valued and due for a correction. Elliott's view was mainly technically based and not based on any synopsis of recent political or economic developments.
